title: Sepher ha-Zohar, Le Livre de la Splendeur Vol. 3 (French, Pauly trans. 1908)
author: Jean de Pauly
description: Sepher ha-Zohar (Le Livre de la Splendeur), Volume 3, a French translation of the Zohar by Jean de Pauly, published in Paris by Ernest Leroux (1906-11) after the translator's death and edited by Émile Lafuma-Giraud. Pauly, a converted Jew of controversial personality, produced the first complete translation of the Zohar into a European language, from the Mantua edition, with notes. The Zohar, the foundational work of Kabbalah written in Aramaic in late thirteenth-century Castile and attributed to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, is a mystical commentary on the Torah. This volume continues the commentary on the weekly portions, revealing the inner life of the sefirot, the divine names, the soul, the mysteries of creation, the Shekhinah and the union of the Holy One and his Bride. Though its accuracy has been criticised, Pauly's translation had wide influence on French esotericism.
